messages.subject: filtering and moving between Cytoscape and rCytoscape (BIG PROBLEMS!)
messages.subject_clean: filtering and moving between Cytoscape and rCytoscape (BIG PROBLEMS!)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Here's my problem: I need to be able use rCytoscape to access a
network that has been created in Cytoscape. Specifically, I need to
use rCytoscape to iteratively filter and select edges back in
Cytoscape, based on edge attributes. (ultimately i need to be able to
turn a bunch of nodes and edges on and off in order to do some
animation -- and doing this manually via Cytoscape's internal filters
is simply not a practical option).

I'm banging my head against the wall at this point because apparently
you can't import graphs into rCytoscape from Cytoscape (you can go the
other way easily enough -- that's the main point of rCytoscape).  You
can port a graph you create in rCytoscape to Cytoscape; you can
subsequently select nodes or edges in that graph in rCytoscape, and
then filter your Cytoscape network based on that selection; but as far
as I can tell, you can't take a pre-existing network that's in
Cytoscape, import edge attributes into rCytoscape, then select edges
based on some criteria, in order to ultimately move back to Cytoscape
to filter your data.

One solution I thought of was to simply output my network from
Cytoscape to a format that I could open in R (absent rCytoscape), but
this is a dead end too, as R (via the igraph package) can only import
GML, not XGMML, which means I can't get my edge attributes into R.

I should say, I've also got an original excel file that contains all
of my nodes, edges, and node and edge attributes.  Might there be a
way I could use this to easily get all this data into R -- all in
order to eventually get my network back into Cytoscape?

Hope this makes sense -- I'm surprised I was able to articulate it at
all, because it's so convoluted!

Any help is greatly greatly greatly appreciated.

Cheers,

Ben

messages.body_plain:
Robert's suggestion should work, existing.CytoscapeWindow works for me.

You could always start from the spreadsheet file.  Here is how I plot from a tab-delmited .txt file (saved from a spreadsheet and imported into R).  Two functions
 plot.cy <http://plot.cy> <-function (cytoscape.file) {
mydata <- new("graphNEL", edgemode='undirected', nodes=as.character(cytoscape.file[, 1]))
# Set up and load all the node attributes
for (i in 2:ncol(cytoscape.file)) {
mydata <- initNodeAttribute (graph=mydata,  attribute.name <http://attribute.name>=names(cytoscape.file[i]), attribute.type='numeric', default.value=0.0)
nodeData (mydata, n=as.character(cytoscape.file[, 1]), attr=names(cytoscape.file[i])) <- as.numeric(cytoscape.file[,i])
}
# load standard edge attributes
mydata <- initEdgeAttribute (graph= mydata, attribute.name <http://attribute.name>='edgeType', attribute.type='char', default.value='undefined')
  mydata <- initEdgeAttribute(mydata, attribute.name <http://attribute.name> = "Weight", attribute.type = "numeric", default.value = 0.0)
return(mydata) }

That loads the node attributes.  For edges, something like this works:
edgeData (subgraph2, as.vector(edgefile$Gene.1, mode="character"), as.vector(edgefile$Gene.2, mode="character"), attr='Weight') <-edgefile$Weight

If you have multiple edges use:
addGraphToGraph (Cy_Wind, subgraph2)

Hope this helps,

Mark Grimes
University of Montana

messages.subject: selecting the nodes connected by selected edges
messages.subject_clean: selecting the nodes connected by selected edges
messages.body_plain:
Benjamin asks:

Is there an easy way to activate the "Select --> nodes connected by
selected edges" feature in cytoscape via rCytoscape?  i didn't see
this in the list of functions, but perhaps i overlooked it?

We forgot to implement this one, along with its companion:  select
edges between selected nodes.  They are both on the todo list, but in
the mean time, here is a workaround.

 - Paul

selectNodesConnectedBySelectedEdges = function (cw) {
  selectedEdges = getSelectedEdges (cw)
  if (length (selectedEdges) == 1 && is.na <http://is.na> (selectedEdges))
    return ()
  tokens = unlist (strsplit (selectedEdges, ' '))
  node.names = intersect (tokens, nodes (cw@graph))
  if (length (node.names) > 0)
    selectNodes (cw, node.names)
  }

messages.subject: new options for export image: pdf & svg
messages.subject_clean: new options for export image: pdf & svg
messages.body_plain:
Jan added two new export options to CytoscapeRPC -- PDF and SVG.  Robert Flight requested them, saying that these formats make for very nice publication-quality images.   Previously, the bit-mapped format PNG was all we had.  I took a quick look at the results of Jan's changes, and the results are beautiful.

I write for a few reasons:

 1) To see if I can persuade :} Jan to add these new options to the existing CyRPC method 'exportView'
 2) To explain how these methods will appear in the RCytoscape API (even if Jan finds my argument unpersuasive)
 3) To explain how these methods can be called right now as long as you install Jan's latest plugin

------ First, I try to make a case for extending the existing CyRPC method.

 We already have the 'saveImage' method:

 setMethod ('saveImage', 'CytoscapeWindowClass',
    function (obj, file.name <http://file.name>, image.type, scale) {
      id = as.character (o...@window.id)
      result = xml.rpc (obj@uri, 'Cytoscape.exportView', id, file.name <http://file.name>, image.type, scale)
      invisible (result)
      })

 called like this

    saveImage (cw, 'xxx.png', 'png', scale=2.0)

 Jan added Cytoscape.exportViewToPDF  and Cytoscape.exportViewToSVG

 I propose that the CyRPC API would be a little simpler if we stuck to only Cytoscape.exportView, but expanded it so that it could accept the two new image.type values:  pdf & svg.  The 'scale' argument would be ignored with the two new image.type values.

---- Second, the upcoming small change to the RCy api, not dependent upon what Jan decides (I can accomodate whatever he chooses):

 saveImage (cw, file.name <http://file.name>, image.type='png'|'svg'|'pdf', scale=1.0)  # 'scale' will be ignored unless image.type is 'png'.

---- Third, here is how to call these methods right now via xml.rpc, directly, as long as you have Jan's latest version of the plugin, available today):

Once you have a CytoscapeWindow object, for example:

 cw <- demoSimpleGraph ()  # makes a 3-node, 3-edge network

Call these lower-level methods to do the export:

 xml.rpc (cw@uri, 'Cytoscape.exportViewToPDF', c...@window.id, paste (getwd(), 'test.pdf', sep='/'))
 xml.rpc (cw@uri, 'Cytoscape.exportViewToSVG', c...@window.id, paste (getwd(), 'test.svg', sep='/'))

Let me know if any of this needs clarification.   After I hear Jan's decision, I will reimplement RCy's "saveImage" method to handle the two new types.

- Paul

Hi Paul,

my first idea was to add the SVG / PDF export functionality to the
exportView funtion. I decided against it because makes no sense to have
a 'scale' parameter for exporting a vector based image.

I could provide an additional exportView function which does not require
the scale parameter but that would mean that the two resulting functions
don't actually do the same. I would prefer fixing it your way but don't
see how it can be done neatly :)

Any suggestions are welcome.

Cheers,

Jan

messages.subject: minor fix to RCy::setCenter -- RCytoscape 1.4.1
messages.body_plain:
I just checked in a minor change to the RCytoscape 'setCenter' method, which re-centers the current network view at the supplied coordiates.  This can be especially handy when creating figures for export:  set the center, set the zoom, and (if you keep those coordinates and scaling factor) you will have reproducible images case you need to reproduce them later.

On the Cytoscape end, canvas coordinates expressed as numerics (Java doubles) are required.  But it is reasonable to think of these coordinates as pixel integers too.  A simple cast ('as.numeric') is now in place.  This should be available as RCytoscape v 1.4.1 at Bioconductor tomorrow, after it builds overnight:

 http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/RCytoscape.html

This fix also includes some bug fixes to the vignette -- pointed out to me by a colleague here at the ISB.

- Paul

messages.subject: new saveImage options: pdf and svg
messages.subject_clean: new saveImage options: pdf and svg
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to prompting from Robert Flight and CytoscapeRPC hooks from Jan, new options to the RCytoscape 'saveImage' method are now available:

  saveImage (cw, filename, 'pdf|png|svg', scale=1.0)

The 'scale' parameter is only meaningful for png images; in that case, it specifies the magnification for your network view before it is rasterized.

When saving to pdf and svg images, that parameter is ignored.  Because RCy now provides a default value, it need not be in your function call:

  saveImage (cw, 'xxx.pdf', 'pdf')
  saveImage (cw, 'zzz.svg', 'svg')
  saveImage (cw, 'yyy.png', scale=2.0)

The only updates Bioconductor permits for released packages are bug fixes.  So version 1.4.1 does not contain the new saveImage options.

The changes ARE in the 'devel' version of RCytoscape, currently version 1.5.2, and with the setCenter bug fix, should be available here tomorrow:

  http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/RCytoscape.html

However, to actually use the new saveImage options, you need Jan's latest jar, version "1.8 testing".  Please let us know if you would like a copy.

Cheers!

- Paul
